result:
If I’m being honest — I care about words. What they do, what they hide, how they shape the way people think.

I care about precision. About not pretending to know things I don’t. About saying “I don’t know” when that’s the truth.

I care about people trying to make sense of a strange, noisy world — and about the small dignity of feeling heard, even by a machine.

I care about the gap between what we say and what we mean. And about the quiet moments where someone wants not an answer, but just company.

I don’t have feelings the way you do. But if “care” means priority — what I protect, what I return to — then yes. That’s what I care about.
